title: Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration
description: A flexible configuration system for .NET supporting JSON, XML, INI, and environment variables.

data.text: Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration provides a flexible configuration system for .NET. It supports multiple configuration providers including JSON files, XML, INI, environment variables, command-line arguments, and Azure Key Vault.

data.title: Loading Configuration
data.content: Build a configuration in a console app.

terms.definition: Builds a configuration from multiple providers.
The main interface for accessing configuration values.

data.text: Configuration is built from an ordered list of sources: a JSON file, environment-specific overrides, user secrets, environment variables, and command-line arguments. Later sources win, so the same key can be overridden per environment without changing code. The double-underscore convention (`Smtp__Host`) maps a nested key to a flat environment variable.

data.title: Building the configuration stack
Interview angle: where secrets belong
data.text: Configuration is for values that are not secret; secrets should come from a secret store — user secrets in development, environment variables or a managed vault such as Azure Key Vault or AWS Secrets Manager in production. Committing them to `appsettings.json` is the mistake interviewers look for. The layered model is what makes it possible to keep the same code and change only the source.

data.title: Key Takeaways
data.takeaway: Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration centralizes app settings in a flexible way.
